scope: Named generative models and closely related speech, retrieval and moderation models in official provider catalogs. Dated snapshots, quantizations and aliases are grouped. Provider access and regional availability vary.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.note: API models and downloadable weights; earlier supported releases remain searchable. Routing aliases and dated snapshots are grouped.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.purpose: OpenAI’s flagship for demanding analysis, research synthesis, and extended agent workflows. Integrates reasoning, software engineering, and computer use to carry complex tasks through to a finished result.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.purpose: Combines reasoning, computer use, and software engineering at a lower cost than Astra. Positioned for substantial professional workloads where throughput and cost matter alongside analytical quality.

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.purpose: Reasoning model for software engineering and multi-step agent workflows, with text and image input. Retained alongside Sol 6.1 for existing deployments and comparative evaluation.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.purpose: Cost-efficient reasoning for focused, high-volume workloads. Intended for repeatable tasks where low latency and operating cost are more important than maximum analytical depth.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.purpose: The GPT-5.6 family’s highest-capability option for professional analysis and agent workflows. Supports persistent reasoning and programmatic tool use across extended tasks.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.purpose: Intermediate GPT-5.6 model balancing inference cost with analytical capability. Supports the family’s tool-based workflows for applications that do not require Sol’s maximum performance.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.purpose: The GPT-5.6 family’s economical option for repeated, well-defined workloads. Trades peak capability for lower processing cost in large-scale deployments.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.purpose: Professional reasoning model combining a million-token context with coding, image interpretation, and computer use. Supports document-intensive work and agent workflows involving multiple tools.

models.name: GPT-5.5 Pro
models.purpose: Higher-compute variant of GPT-5.5 for difficult analytical problems. Prioritizes response quality and precision over the turnaround time and cost of the standard model.

models.name: GPT-5.4
models.purpose: Professional reasoning and coding model with configurable reasoning effort. Remains a lower-cost option for deployments that do not require the latest GPT generations.

models.name: GPT-5.4 Pro
models.purpose: Higher-compute GPT-5.4 variant for problems that benefit from additional reasoning. Designed for deeper analysis, with a higher resource cost than the standard model.

models.name: GPT-5.4 Mini
models.purpose: Compact model supporting coding, computer use, and delegated subtasks. Suited to high-throughput workflows that need tools without the cost of a full-size flagship.

models.name: GPT-5.2
models.purpose: Professional reasoning model with adjustable thinking effort. Supports analytical and coding workloads where an established model version is preferred over a newer deployment.

models.name: GPT-5.2 Pro
models.purpose: Higher-compute GPT-5.2 variant intended to improve precision on difficult professional tasks. Uses more inference resources than the standard GPT-5.2 model.

models.name: GPT-5
models.purpose: Reasoning model with configurable thinking effort for coding and agent tasks. Remains available during its announced retirement period for applications completing migration.

models.name: GPT-5 Mini
models.purpose: Smaller reasoning model for cost-sensitive, high-volume processing. Intended for well-specified tasks where latency and throughput take priority over maximum capability.

models.name: GPT-5 Nano
models.purpose: The smallest GPT-5 variant, optimized for inexpensive, rapid processing. Appropriate for narrowly scoped tasks such as classification and extraction within larger workflows.

models.name: GPT-5 Pro
models.purpose: Higher-compute GPT-5 variant for difficult reasoning problems. Prioritizes consistency and analytical depth over speed, with retirement already scheduled.

models.name: o3-pro
models.purpose: Extended-compute version of o3 for hard analytical problems. Designed to improve reasoning consistency when additional latency and computational cost are acceptable.

models.name: o3
models.purpose: Reasoning model for mathematical, scientific, and coding tasks. Can combine visual interpretation with tool use; newer GPT models now occupy the flagship role.

models.name: GPT-4.1
models.purpose: Non-reasoning model emphasizing instruction following, coding, and long-context processing. Handles large document collections without a separate extended-thinking stage.

models.name: GPT-4.1 Mini
models.purpose: Smaller GPT-4.1 variant for responsive text and code workflows. Retains long-context support while reducing cost and latency relative to the full model.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.purpose: Multimodal model accepting text and images for interactive analysis and content generation. Provides direct responses without the configurable reasoning stage of newer GPT models.

models.name: GPT-4o Mini
models.purpose: Compact multimodal model for focused text and image tasks. Designed for low-cost, high-volume applications rather than extended analytical reasoning.

models.name: GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst
models.purpose: High-capability image generation and editing model. Intended for visually demanding work where composition, instruction fidelity, and detailed revisions matter more than generation speed.

models.name: GPT-Image-2.5 Flare
models.purpose: Faster image generation and editing within the GPT-Image-2.5 family. Balances visual quality with turnaround time for repeated creative production.

models.name: GPT-Image-2
models.purpose: Image generation and editing with flexible output sizes and high-fidelity reference inputs. Supports iterative visual revisions and batch production workflows.

models.name: GPT-Live 1
models.purpose: Full-duplex conversational voice model with expressive speech and interruption handling. Can continue a spoken interaction while a separate reasoning model or agent completes background work.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-2.1
models.purpose: Realtime voice model with reasoning and tool use. Improves recognition of alphanumeric speech, handling of silence and noise, and interruption behavior over Realtime 2.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-2.1 Mini
models.purpose: Distilled realtime reasoning model for voice applications. Provides tool-enabled speech interaction at lower cost and latency than the full Realtime 2.1 model.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-2
models.purpose: Speech-to-speech reasoning model for interactive voice agents. Supports configurable reasoning effort and external tools within a realtime conversation.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-Translate
models.purpose: Streaming speech-to-speech translation for live conversations. Converts spoken language continuously instead of requiring a completed recording before translation.

models.name: GPT-Live-Transcribe
models.purpose: Low-latency streaming transcription for live audio. Supports contextual hints, specialized vocabulary, and expected languages to improve recognition within a particular workflow.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-Whisper
models.purpose: Streaming speech recognition for realtime transcription. Produces text from incoming audio for applications that require incremental transcripts rather than voice generation.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-1.5
models.purpose: Conversational model with native audio input and output. Supports interactive voice applications while later Realtime generations add more advanced reasoning capabilities.

models.name: GPT-Audio-1.5
models.purpose: Audio input and output through the Chat Completions interface. Intended for audio-aware applications that do not require a continuous realtime session.

models.name: GPT-Transcribe
models.purpose: Speech recognition for recorded files and finalized realtime turns. Supports contextual instructions and vocabulary hints for more accurate transcription of domain-specific material.

models.name: GPT-4o Transcribe
models.purpose: GPT-4o-based speech recognition for recorded audio. Converts speech into text; it does not generate conversational responses or identify speakers as a separate output feature.

models.name: GPT-4o Mini Transcribe
models.purpose: Compact speech-to-text model for cost-sensitive transcription. Uses fewer resources than the full GPT-4o transcription model while retaining contextual language recognition.

models.name: GPT-4o Transcribe Diarize
models.purpose: Speech transcription with speaker diarization and segment timing. Separates contributions in multi-speaker recordings and can use reference clips for known speakers.
models.releaseNote: Exact launch date not yet verified against a primary release reference.

models.name: Whisper
models.purpose: Multilingual speech recognition and translation model. Used for recorded-audio transcription, with a broad ecosystem of open-weight and hosted implementations.

models.name: GPT-4o Mini TTS
models.purpose: Text-to-speech model with instructions for vocal delivery. Generates spoken audio from written content, independently of transcription or conversational reasoning.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Cyber
models.purpose: Specialized model for approved vulnerability research and security testing. Available through separately provisioned Daybreak access for authorized defensive engagements.

models.name: GPT-Rosalind
models.purpose: Specialized reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational research. Integrates scientific tool use across chemistry, protein engineering, and genomics through a trusted-access program.

models.name: text-embedding-3-large
models.purpose: High-dimensional text embeddings for semantic retrieval, clustering, and document matching. Produces vector representations for search systems rather than conversational answers.

models.name: text-embedding-3-small
models.purpose: Compact text embeddings for semantic search and similarity matching. Reduces storage and processing costs relative to larger embedding models.

models.name: text-embedding-ada-002
models.purpose: Earlier text embedding model used in established retrieval systems. Produces vectors for similarity search; changing the embedding model generally requires rebuilding the index.

models.name: omni-moderation
models.purpose: Text-and-image classifier for potentially harmful content. Returns category assessments for application safeguards rather than generating or reasoning through a response.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b
models.purpose: Open-weight reasoning model for customizable deployments. The larger release targets stronger reasoning performance where suitable inference hardware is available.

models.name: gpt-oss-20b
models.purpose: Smaller open-weight reasoning model for local or resource-constrained deployment. Enables customization and infrastructure control with lower hardware requirements than the 120B model.

models.name: GPT-5.3-Codex
models.purpose: Coding-specialized reasoning model for extended software-development tasks. Designed for tool-based coding agents; retained during its announced API retirement period.

models.name: GPT-5.4 Nano
models.purpose: Lightweight GPT-5.4 model for simple, high-volume tasks. Supports context compaction, but omits the computer-use and tool-search capabilities of GPT-5.4 Mini.

models.name: GPT-5.1
models.purpose: Reasoning and coding model with configurable thinking effort. Supports existing agent workflows during migration to newer, actively developed GPT generations.

models.name: TTS-1
models.purpose: Low-latency text-to-speech model optimized for speed. Produces spoken audio from text, with fewer expressive controls than newer speech-generation models.

models.name: TTS-1 HD
models.purpose: Text-to-speech variant prioritizing audio quality over minimum latency. Intended for generated narration and other speech output where fidelity is the principal concern.

models.name: GPT-Realtime
models.purpose: Realtime text-and-audio model for conversational applications. Supports a continuous voice session; migration to newer Realtime models is scheduled.

models.name: GPT-Audio
models.purpose: Audio input and output over Chat Completions. Provides request-based audio interaction rather than the continuous session interface of Realtime models.
models.releaseNote: Exact launch date not yet verified against a primary release reference.

models.name: GPT-4o Audio
models.purpose: GPT-4o audio preview for speech input and generated audio output. Supports audio-aware conversations through the Chat Completions interface.

models.name: GPT-4o Realtime
models.purpose: GPT-4o realtime preview for low-latency speech interaction. Supports continuous audio exchange in existing voice applications during migration.

models.name: GPT-Realtime Mini
models.purpose: Smaller realtime model for cost-sensitive conversational voice applications. Reduces inference cost compared with the full Realtime model.

models.name: GPT-Audio Mini
models.purpose: Compact audio model for request-based speech interaction. Provides audio input and output through Chat Completions at a lower cost than the full audio model.

models.name: GPT-4o Mini Realtime
models.purpose: Compact GPT-4o realtime preview for interactive voice applications. Intended for lower-cost deployments that use the earlier realtime interface.

models.name: GPT-4o Mini Audio
models.purpose: Small GPT-4o audio preview for processing and generating speech. Serves request-based audio workflows with lower resource requirements than the full model.

models.name: GPT-Image-1 Mini
models.purpose: Economical image generation and editing in the GPT-Image-1 family. Prioritizes cost efficiency for repeated visual tasks over maximum image quality.

models.name: GPT-Image-1.5
models.purpose: Image generation and editing model preceding GPT-Image-2. Retained for existing visual workflows during its announced retirement period.

models.name: GPT-3.5 Turbo
models.purpose: Legacy conversational text model supporting established chat applications. Lacks the multimodal and extended-reasoning capabilities of newer model families.

models.name: GPT-4
models.purpose: Legacy language model for text analysis and generation. Remains relevant to existing integrations, but is approaching its scheduled API retirement.

models.name: GPT-4 Turbo
models.purpose: Earlier GPT-4 generation supporting text and image inputs. Designed for long-context analysis and generation in applications built before the GPT-4o series.

models.name: GPT-4.1 Nano
models.purpose: Smallest GPT-4.1 variant for rapid, inexpensive processing. Targets tightly specified text tasks rather than extended reasoning or complex tool orchestration.

models.name: GPT-Image-1
models.purpose: First GPT-Image generation for image creation and editing. Maintained for existing integrations while later releases provide the current visual-generation capabilities.

models.name: o1
models.purpose: Earlier reasoning model designed to spend additional computation before responding. Supports difficult analytical tasks but is being retired in favor of later model generations.

models.name: o1-pro
models.purpose: Higher-compute version of o1 for demanding reasoning tasks. Trades inference cost and turnaround time for improved analytical consistency.

models.name: o3-mini
models.purpose: Compact reasoning model focused on mathematics, science, and coding. Offers a smaller inference footprint than full-size reasoning models.

models.name: o4-mini
models.purpose: Efficient reasoning model for mathematical, scientific, and coding tasks. Supports tool-assisted analysis within a smaller model footprint.

models.name: Chat Latest
models.purpose: A moving alias for the Instant model serving ChatGPT. Useful for evaluating the current conversational experience; the underlying model can change without a versioned release.
models.releaseNote: Rolling alias for the current ChatGPT Instant model; there is no fixed underlying model release date.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.note: Public Claude models and restricted research releases. Access restrictions and scheduled retirements are shown on each card.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.purpose: Anthropic’s highest-capability broadly available model for sustained research, coding, and knowledge work. Combines a million-token context with adaptive reasoning for extended, tool-based tasks.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.purpose: Designed for complex judgment and long-running coding or knowledge work. Combines adaptive reasoning with a million-token context, at lower published token prices than Opus 5.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.purpose: Faster, lower-cost complement to Opus 5.5 for well-scoped professional work. Emphasizes debugging, document production, and routine analysis with adjustable reasoning effort.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.purpose: Low-latency model for interactive applications and high-volume processing. Provides reasoning and tool use when response speed and operating cost constrain the workflow.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.purpose: The first broadly available Fable release for extended research and agent tasks. Supports a million-token context and always-on adaptive thinking.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.purpose: Reasoning model for complex coding and knowledge work, with a million-token context. Retained alongside Opus 5.5 for existing deployments and model comparisons.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.8
models.purpose: Opus generation with a million-token context and support for instructions that change during an ongoing task. Designed for extended agent workflows and software engineering.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.purpose: Reasoning model focused on complex analysis and agentic coding. Introduced task-budget controls and a revised tokenizer for more deliberate management of extended work.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.6
models.purpose: Reasoning model for long-horizon agent tasks. Introduced adaptive thinking to adjust reasoning depth to the task rather than requiring a fixed thinking budget.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.5
models.purpose: Model for specialized analysis, software engineering, and advanced agents. Introduced effort controls to trade response thoroughness against latency and token consumption.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.purpose: Balanced model for professional analysis and tool-based tasks. Provides a million-token context with adaptive reasoning enabled by default.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.purpose: Balanced reasoning model emphasizing agentic search and efficient token use. Supports extended thinking and large-context analysis in established workflows.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
models.purpose: Coding and agent model retained during an announced retirement period. Supports extended thinking, tool use, and established software-development workflows.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5.1
models.purpose: Restricted research model with advanced cybersecurity and biological capabilities. Access is limited to Project Glasswing participants; it is not a routine consumer offering.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5
models.purpose: Restricted Mythos generation for approved research participants. Combines a million-token context with adaptive reasoning, subject to stricter access controls than public Claude models.

models.name: Claude Mythos Preview
models.purpose: Restricted preview underlying the earlier Mythos research program. Deprecated in favor of Mythos 5, with its final retirement date still unannounced.

companies.name: Google
companies.note: Gemini API models and managed agents. Preview releases and existing-user restrictions are identified separately from release dates.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.purpose: Google’s leading Flash model for extended software engineering and agent workflows. Processes text, images, audio, video, and PDFs within a million-token context while retaining Flash-class cost efficiency.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
models.purpose: Cost-efficient multimodal model for high-volume work. Designed for responsive processing and routine analysis where throughput matters more than the deepest reasoning available in the Gemini range.

models.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
models.purpose: Flash generation emphasizing software engineering, web development, and tool-based agent workflows. Retained alongside Gemini 3.8 for established applications.

models.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.purpose: Multimodal Flash model for analytical and tool-based workflows. Supports agentic video understanding, in which the model selectively inspects relevant segments instead of processing every frame.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.purpose: Earlier Flash release for high-throughput multimodal processing. Balances reasoning capability and operating cost across text, image, audio, and video inputs.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
models.purpose: Compact Gemini model for fast, economical multimodal tasks. Retained as a supported option for applications built around its established behavior and pricing.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.purpose: Pro-tier reasoning model in public preview for complex analytical and coding tasks. Supports multimodal inputs and external tools; preview availability differs from stable releases.

models.name: Gemini 3 Flash
models.purpose: Public-preview Flash model combining multimodal input with reasoning and tool use. Earlier release retained for existing applications alongside the stable Flash generations.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Live
models.purpose: Realtime audio model for low-latency dialogue and voice agents. Supports interleaved reasoning and asynchronous tool calls without requiring lengthy pauses in conversation.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
models.purpose: Realtime voice model with additional background reasoning. Intended for conversations that require deeper analysis while maintaining an ongoing audio interaction.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
models.purpose: Speech-generation model emphasizing vocal fidelity, expressive delivery, and long-form consistency. Supports nuanced acting and regional dialects for controlled audio production.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS
models.purpose: Cost-efficient speech synthesis for high-throughput production and realtime voice pipelines. Trades the full TTS model’s maximum expressivity for faster, less expensive generation.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
models.purpose: Speech recognition with speaker diarization, word-level timestamps, and vocabulary biasing. Supports multilingual transcription of domain-specific recordings.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Live Translate
models.purpose: Live speech translation through the Gemini audio interface. Designed for multilingual interactions that require continuous translation rather than post-processing a recording.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live
models.purpose: Public-preview audio-to-audio model for voice-first applications. Supports realtime dialogue and tool-connected conversational workflows.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS
models.purpose: Preview speech-generation model for controlled vocal output. Precedes the Gemini 3.8 TTS series and remains available for existing synthesis workflows.

models.name: Nano Banana 2
models.purpose: Gemini image model for generation and conversational editing. Balances image quality with speed, supporting iterative visual production from text and reference images.

models.name: Nano Banana 2 Lite
models.purpose: Lower-cost image generation model for high-volume creative work. Provides the economical option in the Nano Banana 2 family.

models.name: Nano Banana Pro
models.purpose: Image-generation model emphasizing detailed composition and high-fidelity visual output. Intended for demanding creation and editing tasks using text and image references.

models.name: Gemini Omni Flash
models.purpose: Conversational video generation and editing model. Supports video extension, transitions between reference images, and selectable output resolutions.

models.name: Veo 3.1
models.purpose: Video-generation family with synchronized audio and image conditioning. Supports directed video creation from prompts and reference images through preview endpoints.

models.name: Veo 3.1 Lite
models.purpose: Lower-cost Veo 3.1 preview for video generation. Provides a more economical option for repeated production and iteration than the full Veo model.

models.name: Lyria 3.5
models.purpose: Music-generation model producing full songs with vocals and structural control. Accepts text and image prompts and emphasizes coherence over longer compositions.

models.name: Lyria 3 Clip
models.purpose: Music-generation preview for short, approximately 30-second clips. Accepts text and image inputs to guide the musical style and content.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.purpose: Earlier Pro model for extended reasoning and multimodal analysis. API access is limited to existing users while newer Gemini models serve new deployments.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.purpose: Earlier balanced multimodal reasoning model. Remains available to existing users for established workflows, with new deployments directed to later Flash releases.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
models.purpose: Earlier low-cost Gemini model for high-volume processing. Retained for existing users rather than offered as the default for new applications.

models.name: Nano Banana
models.purpose: Original Gemini 2.5 Flash Image model for image generation and editing. Retired endpoint; the later Nano Banana models provide the active alternatives.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash Live
models.purpose: Earlier native-audio preview for realtime dialogue. Supports established voice applications, subject to the provider’s existing-user access restrictions.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash TTS
models.purpose: Earlier Flash speech-generation preview optimized for responsiveness. Produces controlled spoken output from text in existing audio workflows.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro TTS
models.purpose: Earlier Pro speech-generation preview prioritizing output quality. Supports expressive narration and controlled delivery in existing applications.

models.name: Gemini Embedding 2
models.purpose: Multimodal embeddings for retrieval across text and media. Maps content into a shared vector space for search, classification, and similarity analysis.

models.name: Gemini Embedding
models.purpose: Text embedding model for semantic retrieval and document matching. Produces vector representations for search infrastructure rather than natural-language responses.

models.name: Lyria 3 Pro
models.purpose: Music-generation preview for full-length songs. Accepts text and image prompts, offering longer composition than the companion Lyria 3 Clip model.

models.name: Lyria RealTime
models.purpose: Streaming music model for interactive composition. Allows musical direction to change during generation rather than producing a single fixed track.

models.name: Gemini Deep Research
models.purpose: Managed research agent that plans searches, reviews sources, and synthesizes a cited report. Provides a multi-step research workflow rather than a single model response.

models.name: Gemini Deep Research Max
models.purpose: Research-agent variant intended for more comprehensive investigations. Allocates more extensive research effort to source gathering and synthesis than the standard offering.

models.name: Antigravity Agent
models.purpose: Managed development agent combining coding, file operations, search, and browser-based work. Runs multi-step software tasks within a configured execution environment.

models.name: Gemini Robotics ER 2
models.purpose: Embodied-reasoning preview for spatial analysis, task planning, and multi-robot coordination. Combines multimodal perception with tools that connect reasoning to physical actions.

models.name: Gemini Robotics ER 1.6
models.purpose: Robotics reasoning preview for interpreting scenes and planning actions. Supports tool-based task execution in systems that connect the model to a robot controller.

companies.name: Meta
companies.note: Muse products and downloadable Llama families. Previews and self-hosted weights have different access requirements; announced-only models and quantization variants are excluded.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
models.purpose: Meta’s multimodal reasoning model for extended coding and agent workflows. Integrates visual interpretation with tool execution and powers the company’s Muse product ecosystem.

models.name: Muse Image
models.purpose: Image generation and editing with reference composition and iterative refinement. Integrates search and coding tools to support more controlled visual production in Meta products.

models.name: Muse Video
models.purpose: Previewed media model generating video with native audio. Shares the Muse media pretraining base; public availability should be distinguished from the research demonstration.
models.releaseNote: Preview announced July 7, 2026; public availability is not established by the checked source.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.purpose: Downloadable multimodal model with 17 billion active parameters and 128 experts. Offers self-hosted text and image processing where infrastructure control is a priority.

models.name: Llama 4 Scout
models.purpose: Downloadable text-and-image model with 17 billion active parameters and a 10-million-token context. Supports self-hosted document analysis with a smaller hardware footprint than Maverick.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.purpose: Downloadable 70-billion-parameter text model for multilingual dialogue and reasoning. Offers local deployment and customization without relying on a hosted proprietary model.

models.name: Llama 3.2 90B Vision
models.purpose: Larger Llama 3.2 vision-language model for image understanding and textual analysis. Intended for self-hosted multimodal applications with substantial inference capacity.

models.name: Llama 3.2 11B Vision
models.purpose: Smaller Llama 3.2 vision-language model for image understanding. Reduces hardware requirements relative to the 90B variant for local multimodal deployment.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B
models.purpose: Compact downloadable text model for on-device applications. Supports local summarization, instruction following, and tool-oriented workflows under constrained computing budgets.

models.name: Llama 3.2 1B
models.purpose: Smallest Llama 3.2 text model for on-device processing. Prioritizes a limited memory and compute footprint over the capability of larger language models.

models.name: Llama 3.1 405B
models.purpose: Largest Llama 3.1 text model, intended for high-capability self-hosted deployments. Requires substantial infrastructure and can serve research, customization, and model-development workflows.

models.name: Llama 3.1 70B
models.purpose: Mid-sized Llama 3.1 text model balancing capability with deployment requirements. Supports multilingual analysis and dialogue on institution-controlled infrastructure.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B
models.purpose: Compact Llama 3.1 text model for lower-cost local inference. Supports customization and multilingual applications where hardware resources are constrained.

models.name: Llama 3 70B
models.purpose: Earlier downloadable 70B text model for analysis and dialogue. Retained for reproducibility and applications built around the original Llama 3 generation.

models.name: Llama 3 8B
models.purpose: Smaller original Llama 3 text model for local inference and adaptation. Supports established deployments with lower hardware requirements than the 70B variant.

models.name: Llama 2
models.purpose: Downloadable text-model family spanning 7B, 13B, and 70B parameters. Preserved for established integrations, reproducibility, and research on earlier open-weight systems.

models.name: Code Llama
models.purpose: Coding-specialized Llama family spanning several parameter sizes. Supports code generation, completion, and instruction-based programming on self-managed infrastructure.

companies.name: xAI
companies.note: Grok API models across reasoning, media, and speech. Retired endpoints that redirect to newer models are excluded.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.purpose: xAI’s flagship for coding, agent tasks, and knowledge work. Combines text and image input with a 500,000-token context and configurable reasoning effort for sustained analysis.

models.name: Grok 4.6
models.purpose: Reasoning model for software engineering and knowledge work with text and image input. Retains a 500,000-token context for extended tasks and large source collections.

models.name: Grok 4.5
models.purpose: Reasoning model for coding and tool-based professional workflows. Offers adjustable analytical effort to balance response depth against latency and inference cost.

models.name: Grok 4.3
models.purpose: Cost-efficient model with a million-token context and strong tool-calling support. Adjustable reasoning makes it suitable for document-intensive work as well as faster, routine requests.
models.releaseNote: Exact launch date not yet verified against a primary release reference.

models.name: Grok 4.20 Reasoning
models.purpose: Reasoning-enabled Grok 4.20 model for analytical and tool-connected tasks. Provides the deliberative variant of the family for problems that benefit from additional computation.

models.name: Grok 4.20 Non-Reasoning
models.purpose: Direct-response Grok 4.20 variant without an extended reasoning stage. Prioritizes response speed for text generation and well-specified tool workflows.

models.name: Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent
models.purpose: Research configuration using several collaborating agents. Distributes source exploration and synthesis across parallel workstreams rather than relying on a single response trajectory.

models.name: Grok Imagine Image 2.0
models.purpose: Image generation and editing with configurable quality and multiple reference images. Supports visual iteration and composition within the Imagine API.
models.releaseNote: Exact launch date not yet verified against a primary release reference.

models.name: Grok Imagine Image
models.purpose: Earlier Imagine image model for generation and editing. Remains available independently of the retirement of the separate Image Quality variant.

models.name: Grok Imagine Image Quality
models.purpose: Higher-quality variant of the earlier Imagine image model. Scheduled for replacement by Imagine Image 2.0 through automatic request routing.
models.releaseNote: Exact launch date not yet verified against a primary release reference.

models.name: Grok Imagine Video 1.5
models.purpose: Video generation from text, images, or visual references. Supports native 1080p in text-to-video and image-to-video workflows, with optional preset voices.
models.releaseNote: Exact launch date not yet verified against a primary release reference.

models.name: Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0
